name: Titanium.Network
description:
The `Network` module is used to access networking related functionality.

For TCP sockets, see [Titanium.Network.Socket.TCP](api:Titanium.Network.Socket.TCP).

The legacy [Titanium.Network.TCPSocket](api:Titanium.Network.TCPSocket) object is still required
by the [BonjourBrowser](api:Titanium.Network.BonjourBrowser) and
[BonjourService](api:Titanium.Network.BonjourService) objects.

For all other socket needs, use [Titanium.Network.Socket.TCP](api:Titanium.Network.Socket.TCP).

### App Transport Security

Starting with iOS 9, Apple introduced new security and compatibility guidelines for networking
and connectivity, which include:

  * All connections must support TLS 1.2 or greater, and use forward secrecy ciphers supported by iOS
  * Certificates must use at least a SHA-256 fingerprint with either a 2048-bit or greater RSA key,
    or a 256-bit or greater ECC key
  * Application must be compatible with IPv6 DNS64/NAT64 networks as part of App Store submissions

Because of the new requirements, Titanium disables the App Transport Security (ATS)
requirements, which only includes the TLS and certificate cipher requirements,
to allow all connections by default.

If you wish to re-enable ATS, add the `NSAppTransportSecurity` dict to the `ios plist` section
of the `tiapp.xml` file, then add the `NSAllowArbitraryLoads` key and set it to `false`, indicating
that you want to manage your whitelisted URL's yourself.

``` xml
<ti:app>
  <!-- ... -->
  <ios>
    <plist>
      <dict>
        <key>NSAppTransportSecurity</key>
        <dict>
          <key>NSAllowsArbitraryLoads</key>
          <false/>
        </dict>
      </dict>
    </plist>
  </ios>
  <!-- ... -->
</ti:app>
```

Listed below are other guidelines from Apple.

**Avoid hard-coded IPv4 address literals**

Try not to include hard-coded IPv4 address literals in your application, for example, 127.0.0.1.

**Whitelist URLs**

If ATS is enabled and the web service you are trying to contact does not support the new security guidelines,
iOS will not allow you to connect to the service. An error will be returned in the network response
stating the connection failed because it did not meet the ATS policy standards.

To allow the connection, you will need to add
a `NSAppTransportSecurity` dict to the `ios plist` section of the `tiapp.xml` file.
In the `NSAppTransportSecurity` dict, you add the `NSExceptionDomains` dict to whitelist
specific domains.

For more information, see
[iOS Developer Library: App Transport Security](https://developer.apple.com/library/content/documentation/General/Reference/InfoPlistKeyReference/Articles/CocoaKeys.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP40009251-SW33).

Example:

``` xml
<ti:app>
  <!-- ... -->
  <ios>
    <plist>
      <dict>
        <key>NSAppTransportSecurity</key>
        <dict>
          <!-- 1) Default: Disable ATS completely -->
          <key>NSAllowsArbitraryLoads</key>
          <true/>

          <-- 2) Alternative: Define whitelisted domains -->
          <key>NSExceptionDomains</key>
          <dict>
            <!-- Loosen security measure for www.foo.com domain -->
            <key>www.foo.com</key>
            <dict>
              <!-- Set TLS v1.0 as the minimum TLS version -->
              <key>NSExceptionMinimumTLSVersion</key>
              [string](api:Global.String)TLSv1.0</string>
              <!-- Can use other ciphers besides forward secrecy ciphers -->
              <key>NSExceptionRequiresForwardSecrecy</key>
              <false/>
              <!-- Allow HTTP connections -->
              <key>NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads</key>
              <true/>
            </dict>
          </dict>
        </dict>
      </dict>
    </plist>
  </ios>
  <!-- ... -->
</ti:app>
```

**Test IPV6 DNS64/NAT64**

If you submit your application to the App Store, you should setup an IPv6 DNS64/NAT64
network to test your application to verify it is compatible with IPv6.

If you are running macOS 10.11 or greater, you can use your computer to setup a local IPv6 Wi-Fi
network, which requires an Internet connection not through Wi-Fi.

To create the network, from System Preferences, enable Internet sharing with NAT64 network
enabled to share your Wi-Fi connection.

For detailed instructions, see
[Mac Developer Library: Test for IPv6 DNS64/NAT64 Compatibility](https://developer.apple.com/library/content/documentation/NetworkingInternetWeb/Conceptual/NetworkingOverview/UnderstandingandPreparingfortheIPv6Transition/UnderstandingandPreparingfortheIPv6Transition.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP40010220-CH213-SW16).

properties.name: NETWORK_LAN
properties.summary:
A [networkType](api:Titanium.Network#networkType) value indicating that the device is
communicating over a local-area network.
properties.description:
This constant is also a possible value for the `networkType` property of the
[change](api:Titanium.Network#change) event.

properties.name: NETWORK_MOBILE
properties.summary:
A [networkType](api:Titanium.Network#networkType) value indicating that the device is
communicating over a mobile network.
properties.description:
This constant is also a possible value for the `networkType` property of the
[change](api:Titanium.Network#change) event.

properties.name: NETWORK_NONE
properties.summary:
A [networkType](api:Titanium.Network#networkType) value indicating that no
network is available.
properties.description:
This constant is also a possible value for the `networkType` property of the
[change](api:Titanium.Network#change) event.

properties.name: NETWORK_UNKNOWN
properties.summary:
A [networkType](api:Titanium.Network#networkType) value indicating that the
current network type is unknown.
properties.description:
This constant is also a possible value for the `networkType` property of the
[change](api:Titanium.Network#change) event.

properties.name: NETWORK_WIFI
properties.summary:
A [networkType](api:Titanium.Network#networkType) value indicating that the
device is communicating over a WiFi network.
properties.description:
This constant is also a possible value for the `networkType` property of the
[change](api:Titanium.Network#change) event.

properties.name: networkType
properties.summary: Network type value as a constant.
properties.description: One of the `NETWORK` constants defined in [Titanium.Network](api:Titanium.Network).

properties.name: networkTypeName
properties.summary: Network type as a String. Returns one of `NONE`, `WIFI`, `LAN`, `MOBILE`, or `UNKNOWN`.

properties.name: NOTIFICATION_TYPE_ALERT
properties.summary: Constant value for an Alert style push notification.

properties.name: NOTIFICATION_TYPE_BADGE
properties.summary: Constant value for a Badge style push notification.

properties.name: NOTIFICATION_TYPE_NEWSSTAND
properties.summary: Constant value for a Newsstand style push notification. Only available on iOS 5 and later

properties.name: NOTIFICATION_TYPE_SOUND
properties.summary: Constant value for a Sound style push notification.

properties.name: online
properties.summary: Boolean value indicating if the device is connected to the network.
properties.description:
The `online` property is `true` if the device has network access via WiFi,
LAN, or mobile/cellular network.

Note that if the device is connected to a private network without Internet access,
then this property will be `true` as well. This means you cannot assume the device
has Internet access if it's connected to the network.

properties.name: PROGRESS_UNKNOWN
properties.summary: Constant value specifying that the progress of a download can not be calculated.

properties.name: remoteDeviceUUID
properties.summary:
Remote device UUID if the device is registered with the Apple Push Notification
Service, or null if it is not registered.

properties.name: remoteNotificationsEnabled
properties.summary:
Indicates whether push  notifications have been enabled using
[registerForPushNotifications](api:Titanium.Network#registerForPushNotifications).

properties.name: remoteNotificationTypes
properties.summary: Array of push notification type constants enabled for the application.

methods.name: addHTTPCookie
methods.summary: Adds a cookie to the HTTP client cookie store.
methods.description:
On iOS, the cookie will override an existing cookie with the same name, domain and path, if any. The cookie's
`expiryDate` property must be a date later than the creating date, otherwise the cookie will not persist in the
cookie storage.
On Android, any existing cookie with the same domain and name will be replaced with the new cookie. This is a bug
in [BasicCookieStore](https://developer.android.com/reference/org/apache/http/impl/cookie/BasicClientCookie.html)
because based on `RFC6265`, an existing cookie can be evicted and replaced only when it has the same cookie-name,
domain-value and path-value with the new cookie.

parameters.name: cookie
parameters.summary: The cookie to add

methods.name: addSystemCookie
methods.summary: Adds a cookie to the system cookie store.
methods.description:
On Android, [Titanium.UI.WebView](api:Titanium.UI.WebView) uses the system cookie store. Any existing cookie with the same
domain, path and name will be replaced with the new cookie.

parameters.name: cookie
parameters.summary: The cookie to add

parameters.name: type
parameters.summary: Type of service.  Must include the protocol identifier (._tcp).

parameters.name: domain
parameters.summary: Domain to publish the service in.

methods.summary: Returns a decoded version of a URI encoded value.

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: URI encoded input value to be decoded.

methods.name: encodeURIComponent
methods.summary: Returns a URI encoded version of the specified URI component.
methods.description:
On iOS, this also escapes the following characters, which are allowed in a
URL but may not be allowed or desirable inside a path component:

```
!*'();:@+$,/?%#[]=&
```

parameters.name: value
parameters.summary: Input value to be encoded.

methods.name: getHTTPCookies
methods.summary: Gets all the cookies with the domain, path and name matched with the given values from the HTTP client cookie store.
methods.description:
The domain matching and path matching follow `RFC6265`. If name is null, return all the cookies with the domain and
path matched.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.summary: The domain of the cookie to get. It is case-insensitive.

parameters.name: path
parameters.summary: The path of the cookie to get. It is case-sensitive.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The name of the cookie to get. It is case-sensitive.

methods.name: getHTTPCookiesForDomain
methods.summary: Gets all the cookies with the domain matched with the given values from the HTTP client cookie store.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.summary: The domain of the cookie to get. It is case-insensitive.

methods.name: getSystemCookies
methods.summary: Gets all the cookies with the domain, path and name matched with the given values from the system cookie store.
methods.description:
On Android, [Titanium.UI.WebView](api:Titanium.UI.WebView) uses the system cookie store. The domain matching and path matching follow `RFC6265`.
If name is null, return all the cookies with the domain and path matched. The returned cookies only have their
[name](api:Titanium.Network.Cookie#name) and [value](api:Titanium.Network.Cookie#value) properties returned.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.summary: The domain of the cookie to get. It is case-insensitive.

parameters.name: path
parameters.summary: The path of the cookie to get. It is case-sensitive.

parameters.name: name
parameters.summary: The name of the cookie to get. It is case-sensitive.

parameters.summary: Dictionary specifying push-notification related options.

Simple object for specifying push notification options to
[registerForPushNotifications](api:Titanium.Network#registerForPushNotifications).

properties.name: callback
properties.summary: Callback function invoked upon receiving a new push notification.

properties.summary: The `userinfo` dictionary passed to the Apple Push Notification Service.
properties.description:
For more information, see the following item in the iOS Developer Library:

[`application:didReceiveRemoteNotification:fetchCompletionHandler` in the UIApplicationDelegate Protocol
Reference](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiapplicationdelegate/1623013-application)

properties.summary: Boolean indicating if notification was received while app was in background.

properties.name: error
properties.summary: Callback function called when an error occurs during registration.

inlined.name: PushNotificationErrorArg

A simple object passed to the
[registerForPushNotifications](api:Titanium.Network#registerForPushNotifications) error callback.

properties.summary: Error code. Returns a non-zero value.
properties.description:
If the error was generated by the operating system, that system's error value
is used. Otherwise, this value will be -1.

properties.name: success
properties.summary: Indicates if the operation succeeded. Returns `false`.

properties.name: type
properties.summary: The value of this string is always "remote".

properties.name: success
properties.summary: Callback function called when the push registration is successfully completed.

inlined.name: PushNotificationSuccessArg
inlined.summary:
A simple object passed to the
[registerForPushNotifications](api:Titanium.Network#registerForPushNotifications) success callback.

properties.name: code
properties.summary: Error code. Returns 0.

properties.name: deviceToken
properties.summary: The device token which this device was registered for.

properties.name: error
properties.summary: Error message, if any returned.

properties.name: success
properties.summary: Indicates if the operation succeeded. Returns `true`.

properties.name: type
properties.summary: The value of this string is always "remote".

properties.name: types
properties.summary: Array of `NOTIFICATION_TYPE` constants that the application would like to receive.
properties.description:
Setting the `types` property with the [Titanium.Network.registerForPushNotifications](api:Titanium.Network#registerForPushNotifications) method has no effect.

Use the [Titanium.App.iOS.registerUserNotificationSettings](api:Titanium.App.iOS#registerUserNotificationSettings) method to register the notification types to receive.

methods.name: unregisterForPushNotifications
methods.summary: Unregisters the application for push notifications.
methods.description:
Per Apple's documentation, it is rarely necessary to call this method. See:
[unregisterForRemoteNotifications in the UIApplication Class
Reference](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiapplication/1623093-unregisterforremotenotifications)

For example, calling this method would be required if a new version of
your application no longer supports push notifications.
